summary.method: Same prompt, schema, maths and risk checks as the live desk. Point-in-time inputs only. Entry at the first daily close after the news; stops/targets checked on daily closes; round-trip costs charged. Book P&L = R x risk% of book.
summary.caveat: The model may already know how these events played out from its training data, which would flatter these results. Treat this as a test of the machinery and of calibration; the live paper record is the only truly unseen test.

rows.title: Four tankers sabotaged off Fujairah
rows.regime: Heightened Persian Gulf maritime geopolitical risk following tanker sabotage off Fujairah

trades.thesis: Sabotage targeting commercial tankers near Fujairah introduces an immediate transit risk premium on crude moving through the Strait of Hormuz from Persian Gulf states.
Transit disruptions and war-risk insurance hikes in the Persian Gulf directly lift waterborne Brent crude pricing relative to domestic US WTI supply.

rows.title: Front Altair and Kokuka Courageous attacked in the Gulf of Oman
rows.regime: Acute geopolitical escalation in the Persian Gulf transit corridor

trades.thesis: Attacks on laden tankers approaching the Strait of Hormuz elevate Persian Gulf maritime risk and war-risk insurance premiums, which selectively widens waterborne Brent relative to insulated US domestic crude.
Direct kinetic strikes against commercial tankers off the Iranian coast trigger an immediate short-covering bounce in crude, reversing recent heavy trend selling.

rows.title: IRGC seizes the tanker Stena Impero in the Strait of Hormuz
rows.regime: Acute geopolitical escalation in the Persian Gulf following direct state seizure of commercial shipping

trades.thesis: Direct state seizure of a commercial tanker in the Strait of Hormuz will trigger an immediate war-risk repricing in front-month crude as transit risk escalates across Persian Gulf shipping lanes.
Tanker equities will re-rate sharply higher as Strait of Hormuz transit threats trigger spiking war-risk insurance premia and premium chartering rates for non-Persian Gulf routes.

rows.title: Drone and missile strike on Saudi Abqaiq and Khurais (5.7 mb/d offline)
rows.regime: Acute physical supply shock following unprecedented kinetic infrastructure strike in the Persian Gulf

trades.thesis: The loss of 5.7 mb/d of Saudi crude processing capacity at Abqaiq and Khurais is the largest single abrupt physical supply disruption in modern oil history, guaranteeing a sharp geopolitical and physical risk premium re-pricing.

Brent will trade at a sharply higher premium to WTI as international seaborne crude balances bear the direct brunt of missing Persian Gulf volumes, while US domestic balances are sheltered by domestic supply.

rows.title: US strike kills IRGC commander Qassem Soleimani
rows.regime: Acute geopolitical escalation in the Middle East following direct US strike on Iranian military leadership

trades.thesis: The killing of Soleimani creates immediate risk of Iranian military or proxy retaliation against Persian Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, expanding the geopolitical risk premium.
Persian Gulf transit and supply threats directly affect seaborne Brent benchmarks while insulating US domestic WTI, driving Brent-WTI spread widening.

rows.title: Iran fires missiles at US bases in Iraq
rows.regime: Acute geopolitical escalation following Iranian ballistic missile strikes against US military facilities in Iraq.
rows.noTrade: Outright crude longs are withheld because prior escalation events indicate a significant risk of quick price exhaustion if physical oil facilities in Persian Gulf states and Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic are not disrupted.

trades.thesis: Direct state-level strikes elevate perceived shipping and supply risks around the Persian Gulf, widening the sea-borne Brent benchmark premium over landlocked WTI.
Unprecedented direct Iranian missile attacks on US installations prompt immediate safe-haven bid and hedge positioning against wider Middle East conflict.

rows.title: Drone strike on the tanker Mercer Street off Oman
rows.regime: Heightened geopolitical maritime risk following drone strike on commercial shipping in Persian Gulf approaches
rows.noTrade: Refraining from tanker equities (FRO/DHT) due to high equity beta and recent downtrend until fixture rates confirm war-risk premium pass-through.

trades.thesis: The drone attack on the Mercer Street off Oman introduces prompt war risk premium into seaborne crude benchmarks, triggering short-term headline buying.
Seaborne Brent will price in Persian Gulf transit and war-risk insurance premiums relative to inland US WTI crude.

rows.title: Hamas attack on Israel; regional war risk
rows.regime: Geopolitical escalation / regional conflict shock
rows.noTrade: Outright crude longs are withheld because escalation base rates show 5-day and 20-day median Brent returns turn negative unless direct physical oil infrastructure in Persian Gulf states is damaged.

trades.thesis: The outbreak of war in the Levant introduces immediate geopolitical risk premia into waterborne Brent pricing relative to landlocked WTI, driven by proximity to Persian Gulf states and potential shipping tension.
Safe-haven flows will support gold over the coming sessions as market participants hedge against regional contagion across the Middle East.

rows.title: Houthis seize the car carrier Galaxy Leader in the Red Sea
rows.regime: Geopolitical escalation via maritime choke point threat in the Bab el-Mandeb / Red Sea
rows.noTrade: Outright crude oil was not added due to strong existing 20-day downward momentum (-12.5% on Brent) which historical base rates show often reasserts itself past the immediate headline pop.

trades.thesis: The seizure of the Galaxy Leader directly threatens the Bab el-Mandeb maritime corridor, driving up maritime war-risk premiums and setting expectations for potential Cape rerouting that expands tanker ton-mile demand.

Choke point friction in the Red Sea and potential transit risk through the Suez Canal disproportionately impacts European waterborne crude benchmarks relative to landlocked North American supply, widening the Brent-WTI spread.

rows.title: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd pause Red Sea transits; BP follows
rows.regime: Chokepoint transit suspension driving structural ton-mile and regional sweet-sour crude dislocation

trades.thesis: Widespread diversion of crude and commercial traffic away from Bab el-Mandeb toward the Cape of Good Hope adds 10 to 14 sailing days per voyage, tightening effective vessel supply and lifting charter day rates.
Delays to Persian Gulf crude reaching European refiners through the Suez Canal increase spot demand for North Sea and regional Atlantic crudes, widening Brent's premium against US inland barrels.

rows.title: US and UK strike Houthi targets in Yemen
rows.regime: Geopolitical escalation / maritime transit disruption
rows.noTrade: Tanker equities (FRO, DHT, STNG) have already appreciated 13-20% over the past 20 days and show negative median returns in escalation event studies; refined products and gas lack confirmed physical shortages without Persian Gulf export blockades.

trades.thesis: Direct military action in Yemen increases rerouting frequency around the Cape of Good Hope, disproportionately elevating waterborne Brent freight and insurance costs relative to landlocked WTI.

Direct Western military intervention injects an immediate geopolitical risk premium into prompt crude contracts, driving a short-term price spike before longer-term supply realities assert themselves.

rows.title: Houthi missile sets the tanker Marlin Luanda on fire
rows.regime: Geopolitical escalation via kinetic strikes on commercial tankers in the Bab el-Mandeb transit corridor
rows.noTrade: Limiting book risk to two high-conviction relative-value and shipping-specific expressions, avoiding outright crude contracts that already gained over 6% over the preceding five sessions.

trades.thesis: A confirmed missile strike and fire on an active tanker dramatically escalates maritime risk, prompting broad fleet diversions around the Cape that drive up European delivery costs and widen Brent relative to WTI.
Crude tanker equities receive a strong near-term bid as widespread Red Sea avoidance extends voyage lengths via the Cape of Good Hope, tightening effective vessel supply.

rows.title: Iran's drone and missile attack on Israel; IRGC seizes MSC Aries near Hormuz
rows.regime: Acute geopolitical escalation and Persian Gulf maritime interdiction risk
rows.noTrade: Outright crude (Brent/WTI) is withheld: front-month Brent has already rallied +5.89% over the trailing 20 days into this widely anticipated event, leaving high vulnerability to a 'sell-the-news' reversal if strikes inflict minimal infrastructure damage.

trades.thesis: The IRGC seizure of MSC Aries in the Strait of Hormuz and direct Iranian strikes on Israel will widen Brent's premium over WTI as waterborne Persian Gulf transit risk and marine insurance premia are priced directly into seaborne crude.
Direct state-on-state confrontation between Iran and Israel will drive aggressive immediate flight-to-safety flows across global market opens.

rows.title: Israeli strike near Isfahan, Iran
rows.regime: Direct state escalation in the Middle East with heightened Persian Gulf risk premium
rows.noTrade: Outright long crude positions (Brent/WTI outright) are bypassed because historical base rates show headline escalation spikes often give back gains by day 5 unless energy infrastructure in Persian Gulf states suffers demonstrable physical damage.

trades.thesis: Direct military strikes between regional powers disproportionately elevate the geopolitical and shipping risk premium on seaborne crude originating in the Persian Gulf relative to landlocked North American supply.

Direct military engagement between sovereign states triggers a sustained safe-haven bid across broader asset classes over a 3-5 day window while the likelihood of further retaliatory rounds is evaluated.

rows.title: Houthis attack the tanker Sounion (1m bbl) in the Red Sea
rows.regime: Bearish flat price crude regime punctured by acute Red Sea tanker transit disruption

trades.thesis: Attacks on laden crude tankers in the southern Red Sea raise war-risk insurance and reroute westbound crude flows around Africa, structurally widening the prompt Brent premium over US WTI.
Attacks on crude carriers force further Suez diversions around the Cape of Good Hope, boosting ton-mile demand and spot tanker sentiment.

rows.title: Iran fires ~180 ballistic missiles at Israel
rows.regime: Acute geopolitical escalation / state-on-state kinetic conflict in the Middle East

trades.thesis: Direct Iranian missile strikes on Israel trigger an acute risk premium reflecting potential Israeli retaliation against Iranian oil facilities (such as Kharg Island) and heightened disruption risk across Persian Gulf shipping lanes.
Middle East supply disruption risk directly impacts seaborne waterborne Brent while leaving US domestic crude insulated, driving the Brent-WTI spread wider.

rows.title: Israel strikes Iran, avoiding oil infrastructure
rows.regime: Geopolitical de-escalation relief following targeted military-only strike

trades.thesis: Israeli strikes on Iran carefully avoided oil infrastructure and export facilities, removing the immediate tail risk of physical Persian Gulf crude supply disruption and triggering a swift collapse of the geopolitical risk premium.

rows.title: Israel launches strikes on Iran's nuclear and military sites
rows.regime: Acute geopolitical escalation in the Persian Gulf following direct Israeli strikes on Iranian facilities
rows.noTrade: Outright crude was bypassed due to extreme trailing momentum (+11.7% in 5 days), where event studies show post-spike mean reversion over 20-day horizons.

trades.thesis: Direct military confrontation in the Persian Gulf threatens seaborne flows and transit through the Strait of Hormuz, disproportionately lifting seaborne Brent relative to North American WTI. The spread compressed by $1.66/bbl over the past 20 days to $1.25/bbl, creating an attractive entry for risk premium expansion.

Frontline shares have lagged crude's double-digit surge, gaining only 1.32% over 5 days despite surging war-risk insurance and freight premium risks for crude carriers loading in the Persian Gulf. Sustained tension around the Strait of Hormuz will support tanker earnings and sentiment.

rows.title: US strikes Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan
rows.regime: Direct US-Iran military escalation with acute Persian Gulf maritime retaliation risk

trades.thesis: Direct US military strikes on Iranian nuclear infrastructure will drive an immediate geopolitical risk premium into seaborne Persian Gulf-exposed Brent crude, while domestically anchored WTI lags.
Escalating conflict near the Strait of Hormuz will trigger immediate war risk insurance surcharges and panic-chartering, boosting tanker sentiment and fleet utilization.

rows.title: Houthis sink the bulkers Magic Seas and Eternity C
rows.regime: Heightened Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb interdiction risk following confirmed kinetic sinkings of merchant vessels.

trades.thesis: The sinking of two bulk carriers in the Bab el-Mandeb escalates transit risk to extreme levels, forcing residual commercial traffic around the Cape of Good Hope and widening Brent's waterborne premium over WTI.
Direct sinking of commercial ships introduces an immediate freight and war-risk premium into prompt international crude pricing over the weekly trading cycle.
